summary: The EX2 is Geely's second Australian model and its cheapest, a rear-wheel-drive electric light hatch that opened for order in July 2026 at $26,490 before on-road costs. Reviewers rate the packaging highly for the money — 375 litres of boot plus a 70-litre frunk, genuine rear legroom and a cabin that reads above its price — but early drives split on the chassis, with Chasing Cars criticising body control and tyre grip while CarExpert found it agile and fun around town. The bigger caveats are objective: the base car's 252km WLTP range and 14.2-second 0-100km/h, and no ANCAP result at the research date.
pros: Second-cheapest new EV in Australia at $26,490 plus on-road costs, undercut only by the BYD Atto 1 Essential at $23,990
375-litre boot plus a 70-litre frunk beats the Hyundai Inster's 280 litres from a 4,135mm-long body
Rear-wheel drive with multi-link independent rear suspension, rare in a light hatch where the BYD Dolphin and MG 4 Urban rivals are front-drive or pricier
Seven-year unlimited-kilometre vehicle warranty with eight years on the high-voltage battery, matching the Geely EX5
Launch offer running 12 July to 31 August 2026 adds a 7kW home charger (installation excluded) and a free premium paint upgrade
cons: The 60kW Complete takes a claimed 14.2 seconds to 100km/h, which reviewers flag as marginal for freeway merging; the 85kW Inspire is still 11.5s
252km WLTP on the Complete is the shortest range of any EV in this price band — the Inspire's 345km costs $4,500 more
DC charging peaks at just 60kW (Complete) and 80kW (Inspire), and AC at 6.6kW, so it is a poor road-trip car
No ANCAP or Euro NCAP crash rating published as at July 2026, unlike the five-star Geely EX5
Chasing Cars' pre-launch drive found poor body control under brakes and through corners plus noisy, low-grip tyres, a criticism CarExpert's short local drive did not reproduce
